newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec says Tabuchis to resign as advisers.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec says Tabuchis to resign as advisers.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday that former chairman Setsuya Tabuchi and former president Yoshihisa Tabuchi have told the company that they will resign as advisers.
Japan's biggest brokerage has been hit by a scandal in which the company is suspected of illegally providing company money to a corporate client linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.

The two Tabuchis (no relation) resigned their positions in 1991 over a scandal in which, according to Japanese media, Nomura had compensated elite clients for losses and its affiliates had contacts with gangsters.

At Nomura's 1995 annual shareholders' meeting, the two Tabuchis were approved as directors despite heavy public criticism. Earlier this year, they resigned their positions as directors and became advisers to the brokerage amid the latest racketeer and payoff scandal at Nomura.

Yoshihisa Tabuchi's successor Hideo Sakamaki, who stepped down in March, was arrested on suspicion of conspiring with three Nomura executives to give 38.5 million yen to the racketeer Ryuichi Koike in March 1995.
The two Tabuchis were summoned to an upper house committee on Thursday to speak as unsworn witnesses on Nomura's payoff scandal.
